jessica (AE): Kicked off the Quantico POC final burn-in earlier today. Posting the concise readout here so we can turn it into a quote + handoff.

liam (eng-ml): Nice — quick summary pls (QPS, p95/p99, config used).

jessica (AE): Short prompts (<=64 tokens): sustained 400 qps for 15m, med ~55ms, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~220ms.
Long prompts (~512 tokens): sustained 60 qps, med ~320ms, p95 ~790ms, p99 ~1.3s.

omar (eng-platform): Test harness details: ran on a 1-node dedicated A100-style instance (single model replica) with autoscaling disabled. Batching set to "continuous" with target_batch=4, kv_cache enabled.

liam (eng-ml): Model was quantized to 4-bit for throughput runs. We also did an unquantized single-run for quality checks — no regression observed on the provided eval set.

deploy-bot: Load test started by jessica at 2025-11-12T14:03:42Z. Driver: rload v0.9.5.

jessica (AE): Command used: `./rload --target 400 --prompt-file quantico_prompts.json --concurrency 64 --duration 900`

omar (eng-platform): Observed warmup behavior: first 90s had double latency due to cold KV caches. After steady-state, batching reduced per-token CPU by ~28%. We saw tail spikes when two large requests hit same GPU at the same time — mitigated by request queue smoothing.

ryan (security): Quick sec notes for the prospect: they asked about KMS latency impact. We measured end-to-end with KMS envelope decrypt during start-of-session: added ~12ms once per session. We recommended session key caching on client side for high QPS. Also flagged HSM requirement — need follow-up on whether they require attested HSM in Private deployment.

marta (finance): Pricing ask from prospect: they want an E2E monthly estimate for 50M tokens/month with these patterns (80% short, 20% long). Ballpark cost to us for dedicated GPU hours + SW overhead?

liam (eng-ml): Rough from bench: with our quantized profile, short workload effective tokens/sec per GPU ~3.2k tokens/s. 50M tokens/month ~ 17k tokens/hr average -> ~5 GPU hours/day -> ~150 GPU hours/month. Add infra overhead + networking. I'll send a tighter cost model tomorrow.

jessica (AE): Enterprise blockers called out by Quantico: 1) HSM/KMS SLA + proof for key residency, 2) multi-AZ failover testing, 3) contractual latency SLOs for p95 on short prompts.

omar (eng-platform): Multi-AZ failover note: our routing fallback to a compatible quantized variant added ~200ms during failover in the test. We can reduce that by pre-warming a cold standby or using cross-zone warm replicas; tradeoff is ~20% more reserved capacity.

taylor (solutions): For the proposal, we should include two options: (A) Dedicated single-AZ reserved capacity sized to 6 GPUs with canary failover, (B) Multi-AZ active-passive with 8 GPUs reserved (pre-warmed standby). Include expected p95 numbers and incremental cost.

marta (finance): Agree. Also include a short TCO line showing yearly commitment discount vs pay-as-you-go.

ryan (security): I'll draft the security answers re: key handling + audit logs. Need the exact KMS integration name from the prospect (they mentioned Azure Key Vault vs AWS KMS).

jessica (AE): Action items: 1) liam — send detailed perf spreadsheet & token/sec calc (tomorrow EOD). 2) omar — run a multi-AZ failover simulation and post logs (this week). 3) ryan — draft KMS/HSM responses and ask whether attested HSM required (tomorrow). 4) taylor/marta — build two pricing options + TCO (mon).

liam (eng-ml): Will attach perf CSV and the small script used to convert tokens->GPU-hours to the channel when ready.

omar (eng-platform): I'll include the failover log snippet and the command we used to inject the AZ outage: `kubectl cordon --namespace=redwood --selector=zone=us-east-1a` then force traffic to fallback pool.

jessica (AE): Thanks — if we can get the cost + security answers by Monday we can lock a mid-week call with the customer. :thumbsup:

taylor (solutions): I'll prepare a short slide (1-pager) with the latency/throughput summary and the two sizing options.

deploy-bot: Load test finished at 2025-11-12T14:18:32Z. Logs uploaded to https://redwood.internal/logs/quantico/1751112223/run.json

jessica (AE): Great — keeping this thread as the canonical readout. If anyone sees something to add, drop it here.

ryan (security): One more: recommend adding a CP-SSO check on onboarding to capture their key residency selection early.

jessica (AE): Noted — added to the action list. Closing for now, will update with attachments.
